question: Why did Rutherford conclude that the atom contains a very small but massive positively charged nucleus? Give reason based on the scattering of $\alpha$-particles.

options.A: Most alpha particles passed undeflected, proving the whole atom is a solid positively charged sphere.
options.B: Only small-angle deflections show that positive charge is uniformly distributed throughout the atom.
options.C: Rutherford concluded that the nucleus is negatively charged because alpha particles rebounded.
options.D: Only a few alpha particles underwent large-angle deflections or rebounded, requiring a very strong repulsive field confined to a tiny central region. This shows that positive charge is concentrated in a small nucleus; rebounding particles indicate that this nucleus is also massive.
